newsitem.title: USA: Five white separatists indicted in bank robberies.
newsitem.headline: Five white separatists indicted in bank robberies.

text.p: Five members of a white separatist group known as the Aryan Republican Army were indicted Thursday by a federal grand jury on charges of conspiracy to rob banks to fund the group, federal prosecutors announced.
Four of the suspects were in custody and the surrender of the fifth was being negotiated, authorities said.
The five are accused of carrying out seven bank robberines in Ohio, Missouri, Iowa and Wisconsin in 1994 and 1995, and using the proceeds to buy weapons and fund recruiting efforts.
In addition, a release from the office of the U.S. Attorney for Eastern Pennsylvania said, the accused left bombs or decoys inside the banks they had robbed or in getaway cars.
The office also said the defendants used false identities, "safe houses" and police scanners in carrying out the robberies.

Charged in the indictments were Mark William Thomas, of Macungie, Pennsylvania; Peter Kevin Lanagan and Scott Anthony Stedeford, of Ardmore, Pennsylvania; and Kevin William McCarthy and Michael William Brescia, of Philadelphia. The surrender of Thomas is still being negotiated, officials said.
